Good evening, Mr. de Souza. Seven thirty, in the morning. It is new today.
Sorry, can you repeat that, please?
Of course. Seven thirty, not eight. The traffic is very bad after eight.
So, seven thirty, not eight. Is that right? And breakfast?
That is right. Breakfast is from seven, so you have half an hour.
Perfect. And in the afternoon? Is there anything?
Nothing until five thirty. And dinner is at eight, in the evening. Please be early — the restaurant is small.
One more thing. The meeting on Friday — morning or afternoon?
Morning now. On Friday at ten. Not in the afternoon.
So: car at seven thirty, dinner at eight, and Friday at ten in the morning. Thank you. Good night.
The meeting is on Friday, at ten in the morning.
Sorry I am late. I am ten minutes away.

Hi, this is Paul, your driver. This message is about tomorrow. There are two changes. First, the car is at the hotel at seven thirty in the morning, not at eight. The traffic on Thursday is very bad after eight. So, seven thirty, not eight. Second, in the afternoon I am not free at five. I have another car at that time. At five, your driver is my colleague. His name is Tomas. Same car, different driver. Dinner is the same, at eight in the evening, and after dinner I am your driver back to the hotel. Is seven thirty too early for you? Please call me tonight, not tomorrow morning. Thank you, and good night.

Here is my day. It is not difficult. I get up at five thirty, every day. From six to seven I walk. That is my hour, only for me. I have breakfast at seven with my children. I start work at eight thirty, and I stop at six. I do not answer the phone after eight in the evening. On Saturday I work in the morning, but never in the afternoon. On Sunday I do nothing. That is not lazy. It is the reason the other six days are good. I go to bed at ten. That is all. No secret.
Good morning. What time is the car tomorrow? At seven thirty, not at eight? And the meeting is at nine. Is that right? I finish at eleven. See you in the morning.
